top.line: Experts on the record, signed, paid and credited
top.para: Let people who know a subject go on the record on an article with a signed opinion they can withdraw, not a comments section. Identity comes in levels, science already publishes and pays for signed reviews, readers should pay for opinions they value, and idea contributors should share in revenue. Signing is for accountability, not civility.

in-short.line: Signed opinions, levels of identity, payment, shares
in-short.para: Opinions on the record, signed by their holder; disagreement is the point. Identity runs from an anonymous tap to a key with a track record, and existing proofs show less than assumed. Science publishes and pays for signed reviews. Readers should pay for opinions and ideas should earn a share. The evidence on real names is mixed.

not-comments.line: Not a comments section: professional opinions
not-comments.para: Many news sites closed comments: Reuters in 2014, NPR in 2016 with about 19,400 active commenters, the Press Democrat in 2025. What I have in mind instead opens reviews on the record to people who know the subject, who go on the record with a professional opinion rather than a comment.

record.line: A position, reasons, evidence and a signature
record.para: An opinion states a position, the reasons and linked evidence, names the text it is about and is signed by the expert's key. It can be withdrawn, leaving a signed note. Agreement adds a name, not a view; the useful opinion comes from the expert's own angle, and the article can change or a new one follow.

levels.line: Five levels of identity, and proofs' limits
levels.para: Anonymous tap, passkey account, key pair, key bound to a known name, key with a track record. Bluesky domain handles (270,000 accounts by April 2025), Mastodon links back, did:web and signed commits prove control of a domain or account, not who someone is. Keybase's move to Zoom warns against one company owning identity.

science.line: Science signs, publishes and sometimes pays reviews
science.para: F1000Research publishes named reviews, eLife public reviews and assessments, PeerJ review histories. Biology Open pays £220 a review and cut time to first decision from 37.7 to 5.5 working days; The Unjournal pays about $350. A $250 trial made reviews faster, not better. Community Notes ranks by agreement across sides and pays nobody.

paying.line: Readers rate an opinion and pay the expert
paying.para: The reading meter already lets readers pay after reading, with the rating setting the price. The same can work for opinions: marking one insightful pays a little, mostly to the expert. That rewards careful disagreement. I found no news platform paying experts for opinions on articles today; Medium and paid science reviews come closest.

share.line: A share of revenue for the idea's author
share.para: If an article that earns money is built from someone's recorded opinion or idea, they should share in it. Records, graphs and release history make contribution traceable. Publishers already get shares from AI products, 80% of Comet Plus revenue and 50/50 from Gist; this applies the idea to people and ideas.

evidence.line: Real names did not help; stable identities did
evidence.para: Santana found anonymity tied to incivility; Rost and colleagues found named commenters more aggressive; Moore and colleagues, over 45 million HuffPost comments, found stable pseudonyms raised argument quality and real names lowered it; South Korea's real-name law barely helped. So signing is for accountability, payment and track record.

build.line: Keys, proofs, opinion records, display, payment
build.para: Built here: reviews with a reader kind, the passkey vault, a sealing key pair, the meter with ratings and payment, text hashes. Needed: a reader key pair that signs, a domain or DNS proof page, a signed opinion record and withdrawal, opinions shown beside reviews, and payments from ratings and article revenue shares.

limits.line: A proposal; proofs and payment have limits
limits.para: Opinion records, proofs and expert payments are not built. A domain proves control, not identity. Paying makes reviews faster, not better. Measuring whose idea shaped an article is open. Research on identity and civility is mixed and mostly about comments. Some figures are the organisations' own.

sources.line: A voice memo and dated research
sources.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026 and research read that day: Bluesky, Mastodon, did:web, GitHub and Keybase on identity; F1000Research, eLife, PeerJ, Biology Open, The Unjournal and a paid-review trial; Community Notes; Medium, Comet Plus and Gist on payment; and studies by Santana, Rost, Moore and on South Korea.
